newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth to buy Wireless Cable of Atlanta for $43.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth to buy Wireless Cable of Atlanta for $43.5 mln.

text.p: BellSouth Corp. said Monday it had a preliminary agreement to buy cable television firm Wireless Cable of Atlanta for stock valued at $43.5 million.
Under terms of the agreement, BellSouth would swap one-half share of its common stock for each share of the wireless cable TV company.
The deal would bolster the regional phone company's position as it seeks to keep pace in the increasingly competitive communications industry and comes as other Baby Bells are making similar moves.
Wireless Cable holds wireless cable television licenses in the Atlanta area. The company beams programmes by microwave to receivers mounted outside a home or office.
Wireless Cable has 9,000 customers that it serves using analogue wireless technology, but its licenses cover an area of 900,000 households.

BellSouth said it plans to provide wireless cable services to Atlanta using so-called digital Multichannel Multipoint Distribution System, which gives the potential to beam 100 channels to the home, including some relayed from satellites.

"Today's announcement means that our customers in the Atlanta area are one step closer to a competitive alternative to their existing cable services," said William Redderson, group president for long distance and video for BellSouth.
The Atlanta-based regional Bell company has two other wireless cable deals in the pipeline.

It is currently negotiating a deal to buy the wireless cable rights in New Orleans for $12 million, and in September National Wireless Holdings Inc. of Miami said it was in talks to be acquired by BellSouth for $48 million.
A number of regional Bells, including Nynex Corp., Bell Atlantic Corp. and Pacific Telesis Group have also previously invested in wireless cable.

The Bells plan to add video services to their current communication and entertainment packages to help bolster market share in advance of the wide-open competition expected to be unleashed by the Telecommunications Act of 1996.
Analysts say packages which include entertainment should command higher profit margins and suffer less customer turnover than communication services alone.
In Nasdaq trading Wireless Cable stock rose $1.50 to $16.50, while BellSouth stock gained $1 to $39.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
